{{About|features that are not yet in a release|released versions|Version history}}
This page collects features of [[Matcha Flavoured]] that are in development or planned, as recorded in the repository's <code>docket_and_checklist.md</code> and in-development <code>changelog.md</code>, the developer's <code>my_current_and_future_plans.md</code> and the README, in the code on the repository's <code>26.3-indev</code> branch, and in the developer's videos. None of it is in the current release, {{Version|{{Current version}}}}, and plans may change or be dropped. The docket was deleted from the main branch in that release, so the plans under "Other plans" are as it last stood in {{Version|1.12.8-beta}}; the <code>26.3-indev</code> branch has a newer copy.

The {{Version|1.12.9}} release notes say the pack is "on break": the developer will not add more features for some time. They plan to port the pack when the next ''Minecraft'' drop comes out and then to redo the [[freezing water]] effect, since the game now has a freezing effect, and say that this should be the only real change until they are ready to add more. They will make a new video when more is being added, and future versions will have a "recap" changelog of everything added since the last release.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.9|quote=I will not add anymore features to matcha for some time. I do want to port when the new drop comes out, and when it does I'm going to re-do the frozen water effect since we now have access to the freezing effect.}}</ref>

== Next update ==
{{Planned|type=section}}
=== Structure update ===
The developer plans a structure update that will move the [[Abbey]] and [[Papal Outpost]] over to the new namespace, revisit the chest, spawner and village loot tables (village loot has been empty in the 26.3 releases since the 1.12.3 alpha for 26.3, and is to return nerfed), and possibly bring back the loot of mobs from [[spawner]]s.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.3|quote=The Abbey and Papal Outposts have not been moved over yet.}}</ref>

=== Steel lanterns ===
The 1.12.8-beta release notes, and the in-development changelog before them, list lanterns that can be crafted from [[Steel Alloy|steel]], by Internet-Hyena, but the lantern recipe in the pack is still the vanilla one, made from iron nuggets.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.8-beta|quote=Lanterns can now be crafted from Steel}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/crafting/lantern.json}}</ref> Buckets made of copper instead of iron, listed in the in-development changelog before 1.12.8-beta, are no longer mentioned there.

=== Animal ecology ===
{{Upcoming|type=section}}
The next update, called "Update Ecologic" in the in-development changelog, reworks chickens, pigs and cows so that they change the ground around them and reward players who look after them. An animal whose needs are met becomes "happy" and gives unique loot, more loot, or does its work more often.<ref name="eco-changelog">{{Source|changelog.md|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref> The work is on the repository's <code>26.3-indev</code> branch. The developer showed it in a video in November 2026 and called it unfinished: "this design that I'm mentioning is is not finalized. I still have a lot to do."<ref>{{Cite video|id=OVaAoRrIuu0|title=Warnings, Concerns, and Advice {{!}} Appendix|quote=I'm going to this design that I'm mentioning is is not finalized. I still have a lot to do.}}</ref> Sheep get a home like the others but are otherwise unchanged; the developer asked for ideas for them and is thinking about goats.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/sheep/set_home.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref><ref>{{Cite video|id=OVaAoRrIuu0|title=Warnings, Concerns, and Advice {{!}} Appendix|quote=So if you have ideas for sheep, let me know like what they would do for the local ecology.}}</ref>

'''Homes.''' Every chicken, pig, cow and sheep that has no home gets one where it stands, and from then on stays near it: within 21 blocks for a cow, 13 for a pig or sheep, and 11 for most chickens. Feeding a pig food that doesn't breed it moves its home to the place it was fed; the changelog says animals in general "tend to stick around where they were last fed". The range from which food in a player's hand draws animals is raised to 15 blocks for cows and 20 for the others, to make it easier to lead them home.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/animal/set_wild_animal_homes.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/cow/set_home.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/pig/fed_effects.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref> Breeding changes with it: cows are bred with hay bales, and pigs only with golden carrots or golden apples. Other pig food (carrots, potatoes, beetroots, apples, sweet berries, meat and eggs), wheat for cows and chicken seeds no longer put the animal in love mode, but shorten the wait before its next dig, graze or peck.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/tags/item/cow_food.json|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/pig/forbid_breeding.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/chicken/forbid_breeding.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref>

==== Chickens ====
Chickens no longer spawn naturally in most biomes; the exceptions are beaches, stony shores, mangrove swamps and jungles, where the new variants take the place of the game's own in their habitats.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/worldgen/biome/beach.json|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/chicken_variant/duck.json|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref> Wild birds come from roosts instead: 13 kinds of small structure, each generating in its own biomes. Most have birds already in them: [[bobwhite]]s in plains, seagulls on beaches, ducks in swamps, and the game's chicken variants in meadows, savannas, dappled forests, dark forests and old growth taigas. The forest, birch forest, taiga, snowy taiga and cherry grove roosts have no birds yet.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/worldgen/structure_set/chicken_roosts.json|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/structure/chicken_roosts/plains/1.nbt|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/structure/chicken_roosts/swamp/1.nbt|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref> Roost birds have personalities that change how far they wander and what they drop:<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/chicken/find_roost/check_home.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/loot_table/gameplay/chicken_lay/seagull.json|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref>
* '''Mama''': stays within 2 blocks of its nest and can lay 1–4 eggs at a time.
* '''Curious''': wanders up to 21 blocks from home. A curious seagull mostly brings up seeds, fish bones and string, and sometimes trinkets such as gold nuggets, raw iron, lapis lazuli, string, an emerald or a disc fragment.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/loot_table/gameplay/chicken_lay/scavanged_chicken_loot.json|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref>
* '''Nest-maker''': has no home, moves faster, and after 10 to 20 minutes makes a nest on grass, dirt or farmland. The block becomes a dirt path with short dry grass on it, two chicks hatch (none yet for ducks), and the bird becomes a mama.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/chicken/chicken_nest.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/chicken/nest/make_nest.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref>
* '''Rascal''' (seagulls only): fast, and brings up only bone meal, 2–6 at a time.
Every 5 to 10 minutes a bird pecks at the ground under it (grass, mycelium or farmland; sand, red sand or gravel for seagulls; ducks dive in water) and drops something from its species' table: usually an egg or a feather, or its personality's loot. Every 400 to 600 seconds (about 7 to 10 minutes) it also plants grass on a random block next to it or under it: short grass grows into tall grass, and a bare grass block, dirt, mud, moss block or farmland grows short grass (farmland turns to dirt). Ducks in water plant seagrass.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/chicken/chicken_gift.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/chicken/plant/plant_grass.macro.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref> The developer added the planting so that grass would grow on its own.<ref>{{Cite video|id=OVaAoRrIuu0|title=Warnings, Concerns, and Advice {{!}} Appendix|quote=I needed a way to have grass grow on its own. And obviously it would be insane to put marker entities under each block}}</ref> Chickens no longer breed or give live birth; new ones come from thrown eggs and nests.<ref>{{Cite video|id=OVaAoRrIuu0|title=Warnings, Concerns, and Advice {{!}} Appendix|quote=For chickens, you just crack their eggs or you let them eat some wheat.}}</ref> An adult chicken (not a seagull, duck or mama) that pecks where a wheat or beetroot crop grows eats it and turns into a nest-maker that nests within 30 seconds, so chickens let into a field multiply.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/chicken/eat/eat_block.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref> Chickens no longer drop feathers when killed.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/entities/chicken.json|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref>

The docket's chicken overhaul plans that are not yet in the code include a way for the [[Farmer|farmer]] to sell and "breed" personalities, a farmer hat made from wheat, and a check against chickens packed too tightly onto hoppers.<ref>{{Source|docket_and_checklist.md|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref> Its earlier plan for nest-makers to hatch three chicks became two in the code.

==== Pigs ====
Every 5 to 10 minutes a pig roots in the block under it. On a grass block, rooted dirt, podzol, mycelium, gravel, sand or soul sand it digs the block up, turning it into dirt (soul sand into soul soil), and drops an item from that block's table: mostly mushrooms and shelf mushrooms from grass and mycelium, flint and raw ores from gravel, coral fans and kelp from sand, and fungi and nether wart from soul sand.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/pig/pig_gift.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/pig/dig/dig_block.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/loot_table/gameplay/pig_gift/grass_block.json|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref> The digging began with a change by Internet-Hyena, made because meat is of little use in the pack while mushrooms are needed and hard to grow.<ref>{{Cite video|id=OVaAoRrIuu0|title=Warnings, Concerns, and Advice {{!}} Appendix|quote=pigs in Matcha are pretty useless because meat isn't very useful. And I made it so that pigs dig up mushrooms since people need mushrooms.}}</ref> On [[mud]] or muddy mangrove roots a pig plays instead: it becomes muddy, with its own muddy texture, and turns the block into dirt. A muddy pig digs every 80 to 150 seconds, and only a muddy pig can dig up the rarest finds: truffles, a raw silver nugget, a turtle shell or a dried ghast. It stays muddy for 15 to 20 minutes (longer if it is standing on mud when the time runs out), or until it goes into water or a player uses a water bottle on it.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/pig/play/get_muddy.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/pig/pig_clean.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/pig/water_bottle_clean_effects.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref> A pig that roots where carrots, potatoes or a mushroom grow eats the plant, and an adult then has two piglets, so pigs let into a field multiply.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/pig/dig/eat_block.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref>

==== Cows ====
Cows graze every 2½ to 5 minutes when they stand in grass, eating tall grass down to short grass and short grass away, and each bite adds one bottle of milk to the cow's reserve.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/cow/cow_graze.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/cow/graze/graze_block.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref> A new block, the '''trough''', is crafted from a hay bale above a cauldron and placed as a cauldron filled with hay; its name has no English text yet.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/crafting/trough.json|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/cow/trough/check_trough_placement.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref> Placing one makes it the home of every cow within 50 blocks, and they walk to it. Cows that reach the trough get hungry and eat a hay bale or wheat crop in front of them, but only while a player is within 40 blocks. Feeding a cow by hand adds no milk: a hay bale breeds it, and wheat only shortens the wait before its next graze. A hay bale adds 10 to the milk reserve and is used up; wheat adds 5 when fully grown and 2 otherwise, and is replanted. The cow then wanders up to 48 blocks away.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/cow/trough/set_all_nearby_cow_home.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/cow/trough/update_nearby_cows.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/cow/eat/eat_block.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref> If its next graze is at least 8 blocks from a trough it becomes happy for about two hours, after which it returns to the trough; if it grazes within 7 blocks, it becomes sad.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/cow/update_happiness.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref> A happy cow drops 1–3 wagyu beef and more leather when killed.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/entities/cow.json|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref> Cows can be milked with a glass bottle, which takes one unit of the reserve and gives a [[milk bottle]], or with a bucket, which takes four; a cow with no milk left is hurt a little and gives the empty container back.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/cow/milk_cow_with_bottle.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/cow/milk_cow_with_bucket.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref> In the video the developer says a cow gains one bottle per grass and nine per hay bale, and the changelog says 9 for a hay bale and 3 for wheat, but the code gives the numbers above.<ref>{{Cite video|id=OVaAoRrIuu0|title=Warnings, Concerns, and Advice {{!}} Appendix|quote=they get one milk bottle per grass they munch on, and they get nine milk bottles when they eat a hay block.}}</ref>

==== Limits and design ====
''Minecraft'' 26.3 stops the random wandering of persistent animals when no player is nearby, as it already did for other mobs. The developer found no way around this in a data pack, so the animals wander, and find their way back home, only while a player stays close to them.<ref name="eco-changelog" /><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/cow/cow_eat.mcfunction|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref> In the video they asked for help: "If you know of a way to enable animal pathing with data packs, only data packs, please let me know."<ref>{{Cite video|id=OVaAoRrIuu0|title=Warnings, Concerns, and Advice {{!}} Appendix|quote=If you know of a way to enable animal pathing with data packs, only data packs, please let me know.}}</ref> The design is meant to make the world near the player feel alive, not to simulate animals in far-off chunks: "This is not a simulation."<ref>{{Cite video|id=OVaAoRrIuu0|title=Warnings, Concerns, and Advice {{!}} Appendix|quote=We just need to make it so that if the player is nearby, some things change. That's all.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite video|id=OVaAoRrIuu0|title=Warnings, Concerns, and Advice {{!}} Appendix|quote=This is not a simulation. We do not need to worry about every population dynamic}}</ref> The developer would deal with performance after the design proves itself, and doesn't expect players to learn every rule: technical players will look them up, and casual players who keep their animals in a pen already get most of the benefit.<ref>{{Cite video|id=OVaAoRrIuu0|title=Warnings, Concerns, and Advice {{!}} Appendix|quote=If they are a technical player who's invested in those things, they will look at the wiki.}}</ref> They warned that such features easily become annoying, that being annoying "in a good way" is acceptable, and that only playtesting finds the line; some block changes that sounded good in theory were "just not fun".<ref>{{Cite video|id=OVaAoRrIuu0|title=Warnings, Concerns, and Advice {{!}} Appendix|quote=Determining the line between something being annoying in a bad way and being annoying in a good way is really going to come down to play testing.}}</ref> A bucket counts as cow food in the code, but cows only let themselves be milked with it; the developer would like them to eat it and asked for a way.<ref>{{Cite video|id=OVaAoRrIuu0|title=Warnings, Concerns, and Advice {{!}} Appendix|quote=I set buckets to be cow food, but they won't eat it.}}</ref>

The same branch also gives sugar cane a new model and textures, so that it no longer looks like bamboo, and lets it grow on clay, mud and muddy mangrove roots.<ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/minecraft/models/block/sugar_cane.json|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/tags/block/supports_sugar_cane.json|at=52de204ea52e49cb94a1f210c2518fd5dae09b2f}}</ref> The developer is not yet sure about the look: "I'm going to have to sit with it."<ref>{{Cite video|id=OVaAoRrIuu0|title=Warnings, Concerns, and Advice {{!}} Appendix|quote=I'm going to have to sit with it. I do think I like it, but you know, we'll see.}}</ref>

=== Other plans ===
The docket lists these as planned for later updates:<ref>{{Source|docket_and_checklist.md|at=58e88dcec369fe3293fb25a15214249d116a100e}}</ref>
; Aspects
: Post-End enchanting that extracts an alloy's intrinsic as an "aspect", using a withered heart and dragon's breath. Planned pairings: bronze ([[Hepatizon equipment|hepatizon]]) gives Efficiency, [[Steel equipment|steel]] Unbreaking, [[Electrum equipment|electrum]] Fortune III, netherite ([[Adamant equipment|adamant]]) smelting, and [[Shakudo equipment|shakudo]] Silk Touch or life steal. An Unbreaking enchantment from the Wither's heart is also planned, and Protection may be replaced by more specific protections.
; Copper intrinsic
: A "conductive" intrinsic for copper armor that draws aura-based effects such as [[warding]] onto itself and nullifies them. The notes suggest players may need more pieces than zombies for full immunity.
; Difficulty scaling
: The number of hearts lost on [[death]] would depend on how many hearts the player has: 1 heart at 10 or more, 2 at 20 or more, 3 at the maximum, plus one more on Hard.
; World generation
: Rarer diamonds, portal structures by TankyAibem and Linkershim, polished villages, and a better [[Abbey]].
; Advancements
: "Echoes" (restore an echo shard's memory), "Child of Moros" (smith a full adamant set) and "Harbinger of Fate" (smith adamant elytra).
; Low-priority bugs (see also [[Known bugs]])
: Keep structures out of the safe-surface spawning check and fix Trailblaze's speed boost on mud brick slabs while running. A third, replacing the toolsmith's gift of stone tools, was done in {{Version|1.12.9}}, whose toolsmith gives [[Jewelry|earrings]] instead.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/hero_of_the_village/toolsmith_gift.json}}</ref>
; Language
: Descriptions for each difficulty in the options menu.

== Stretch goals ==
{{Planned|type=section}}
The docket's back-burner list includes:<ref>{{Source|docket_and_checklist.md|at=58e88dcec369fe3293fb25a15214249d116a100e}}</ref>
* Foods: potatoes with molasses, French fries, jam bread, a secret meal using fermented spider eyes, and a bag of sugar.
* Craftable Thorns.
* More fishing junk from specific biomes (cinnabar, sulfur, dripstone, raw copper, raw gold, disc fragments), and more resin from pale garden fishing.
* Alloy shields: steel with high durability, shakudo blocking splash potions, hepatizon without the movement penalty, electrum damaging undead attackers, and adamant damaging any attacker.
* Better loot in cold biomes and oceans to balance freezing water, and fewer obols in chests, especially in trial chambers.
* Recipes or hints in abandoned camp loot, cats traded by farmers, and a wandering trader that sells more than village maps.
* Copper horns re-added, using sheet music found as treasure.
* Dense poplar forests and swampier swamps.
* Advancements for reaching full health and for crafting a secret weapon.
* Textures: beds, boats with chests, an eye-themed ender chest, and biome sprites for the pale garden, deep dark and sulfur caves.
* Villages that match villager stories, knowledge books, pottery sherds for enchantments, archaeologist maps based on books (such as Paradise Lost leading to the Abbey), upgraded horns, and a redesigned Abbey and papal outpost.
* Ore generation: more coal in swamps, sulfur in sulfur caves and iron in cold biomes.

== Longer-term plans ==
{{Planned|type=section|source=my_current_and_future_plans.md}}
The developer's plans file describes 1.12.2 as a user-experience update centered on the death system, with further features moved to later updates. It lists as done: the Wither removing hearts on hit, nastier wither skeletons, Wither spawn requirements, and [[Sacred texts|Paradise Lost and The Divine Comedy]] no longer giving hearts. Dynamic heart loss was postponed.<ref>{{Source|my_current_and_future_plans.md}}</ref> The developer planned a break after this update to work on videos, art and a new Abbey.

Further ideas in the file:
* A reworked [[Wither]] fight, modelled on a boss that summons allies, with an attack that removes a heart without killing the player. The Wither would be summonable only in one structure, or only under open sky above a certain height.
* [[Hell]] locked behind a structure, possibly the revamped Abbey, after which all portals would work. The aim is to slow progression and give players reasons to stay in Hell longer.
* Enchantments: removing Protection and Sharpness in favor of specific, mutually compatible alternatives, and an Unbreaking enchantment crafted from the Wither's heart.

The README's queue adds:<ref>{{Source|README.md}}</ref>
* All enchantments working like warding, so that two books of the same level cannot be combined into a higher level.
* Reworks of electrum and adamant, including removing Divinity from adamant tools (done in 1.12.1-alpha), and possibly splitting electrum into two alloys.
* An adventure rework in which reaching [[the End]] requires visiting every main overworld structure, each leading to the next through a [[Sacred texts|sacred text]] traded for a map. The [[Mouthpiece|mouthpiece]] and [[Archaeologist|archaeologist]] would both trade sacred texts. The developer asked for feedback on this idea.
